mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes?

options.A: Alkanes contain only single bonds; alkenes contain at least one double bond; alkynes contain at least one triple bond.
options.B: Alkanes contain double bonds; alkenes contain triple bonds; alkynes contain single bonds.
options.C: Alkanes have triple bonds; alkenes have single bonds; alkynes have double bonds.
options.D: All three have the same type of carbon‑carbon bonds.

mcqs.answer: Alkanes contain only single bonds; alkenes contain at least one double bond; alkynes contain at least one triple bond.
mcqs.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with only C–C single bonds (general formula CnH2n+2). Alkenes are unsaturated and possess at least one C=C double bond (CnH2n). Alkynes are also unsaturated and contain at least one C≡C triple bond (CnH2n‑2). The other options mix up these definitions.

mcqs.question: Methane (CH₄) is the first member of the alkane homologous series. Which compound is the third member of this series?
mcqs.explanation: In a homologous series each successive member differs by a –CH₂– unit. Starting from methane (C₁H₄), adding two carbons and four hydrogens gives ethane (C₂H₆) as the second member and propane (C₃H₈) as the third. Hence propane is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Which of the following shows the correct simple structural formula for 2‑butene?
mcqs.explanation: 2‑Butene has four carbon atoms with a double bond between the second and third carbon atoms, giving the formula CH₃‑CH=CH‑CH₃. Option B is 1‑butene, C is 1‑butene with the double bond at the end, and D represents an alkyne (but‑2‑yne).

mcqs.question: A student is asked to identify a saturated hydrocarbon among the following compounds. Which one is saturated?
mcqs.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) contain only single C–C bonds and follow the formula CnH2n+2. Among the options, only butane (C₄H₁₀) satisfies this formula. The others are unsaturated: ethylene (alkene), propene (alkene), and acetylene (alkyne).

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes unsaturated hydrocarbons?

options.A: All hydrocarbons with the formula CnH2n are saturated.
options.B: Hydrocarbons containing at least one double or triple bond are unsaturated.
options.C: Alkanes are unsaturated because they have only single bonds.
options.D: Saturated hydrocarbons must contain a double bond.

mcqs.answer: Hydrocarbons containing at least one double or triple bond are unsaturated.
mcqs.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons possess one or more multiple bonds (C=C or C≡C). Alkenes (C=C) and alkynes (C≡C) are unsaturated. Option A is false because CnH2n corresponds to alkenes (unsaturated). Options C and D incorrectly define saturation.

mcqs.question: A hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C₅H₈. Based on this formula, to which class does it belong?
mcqs.explanation: For alkanes: CnH2n+2 → C₅H₁₂. For alkenes: CnH2n → C₅H₁₀. For alkynes: CnH2n‑2 → C₅H₈. The given formula matches the alkyne pattern, so the compound is an alkyne. Aromatics have different formulas and are not considered here.

mcqs.question: Considering the first three members of the alkane (C₁‑C₃), alkene (C₂‑C₄), and alkyne (C₂‑C₄) homologous series, which statement correctly compares their boiling points?

options.A: For the same number of carbon atoms, alkanes have lower boiling points than alkenes, which are lower than alkynes.
options.B: For the same number of carbon atoms, alkanes have higher boiling points than alkenes, and alkenes have higher boiling points than alkynes.
options.C: Boiling points are the same across all three series for a given carbon number.
options.D: Alkynes always have the highest boiling points regardless of carbon number.

mcqs.answer: For the same number of carbon atoms, alkanes have higher boiling points than alkenes, and alkenes have higher boiling points than alkynes.
mcqs.explanation: Within a homologous series, boiling point rises with molecular mass. Between series, saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) experience stronger London dispersion forces than unsaturated ones with the same carbon count, so alkanes boil at higher temperatures than alkenes, which in turn boil higher than alkynes. Options A, C, and D contradict this observed trend.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is the correct skeletal structural formula for 2‑methyl‑1‑butene?
mcqs.explanation: 2‑Methyl‑1‑butene has a four‑carbon main chain with a double bond at carbon‑1 and a methyl substituent on carbon‑2. The correct skeletal representation is CH₂=C(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₃ (option A). Option B places the double bond at carbon‑2, option C gives a different connectivity, and option D represents 3‑methyl‑1‑butene.
